market.title: EU Instant Payments Mandate Transforms Corporate Payments
market.summary_short: A new EU regulation mandates that all EU/EEA banks must offer instant payments 24/7/365. This significant shift will profoundly impact corporate liquidity management and payment processing strategies.
market.summary_detail: The European Union's Instant Payments Regulation, with key implementation phases starting in early 2025 for receiving and early 2027 for sending, requires all banks within the EU/EEA to process instant credit transfers within 10 seconds, irrespective of the time or day. This initiative aims to accelerate the adoption of real-time payments across Europe, making them as accessible and affordable as traditional credit transfers. Corporates are urged to adapt their treasury systems and processes to leverage these faster settlement times, which promise improved cash flow management and reduced payment delays. The regulation also includes crucial provisions for checking payee details (Verification of Payee, VoP) to enhance fraud prevention.
key_points: Mandatory instant payments for all EU/EEA banks.
Effective early 2025 (receiving), early 2027 (sending).
Payments must be processed within 10 seconds, 24/7/365.
Includes mandatory payee verification (VoP) for fraud prevention.
market.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus must ensure full compliance with the EU Instant Payments Regulation, offering seamless real-time payment initiation and receipt for its CEE corporate clients. Integrating robust VoP capabilities will be crucial for enhancing fraud prevention and building client trust.

market.title: EBICS 3.0 Adoption Critical for Secure Corporate Connectivity
market.summary_short: German banks are actively promoting the wider adoption of EBICS 3.0 for secure corporate-to-bank communication. This updated standard offers enhanced security features and new functionalities like real-time payment status updates.
market.summary_detail: EBICS 3.0, the latest iteration of the Electronic Banking Internet Communication Standard, is rapidly becoming the preferred channel for secure corporate-to-bank communication, particularly in Germany and increasingly across the broader European market. It introduces significant improvements over previous versions, including stronger encryption protocols, support for larger file sizes, and the capability to exchange real-time status messages for payments. Corporates are strongly encouraged to migrate to EBICS 3.0 to benefit from these enhanced security features and to prepare their systems for future innovations in payment processing and reporting. The standard also fully supports ISO 20022 XML messages, aligning perfectly with ongoing European payment modernization efforts.
key_points: EBICS 3.0 is the latest secure bank communication standard.
Offers stronger encryption and support for larger file sizes.
Enables real-time payment status updates for corporates.
Fully supports ISO 20022 XML messages for data exchange.
market.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus already supports EBICS v2.5 and v3.0. Promoting and ensuring seamless EBICS 3.0 connectivity is vital for RBI's German and CEE corporate clients, especially for robust Host-to-Host (H2H) integration and comprehensive ISO 20022 compliance.

The IPR, in particular, mandates the offering of instant payments, which will significantly alter payment flows and liquidity needs, requiring banks to ensure robust real-time liquidity management capabilities.

regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) issued version 7.0 of its Fraud Taxonomy, which will become effective on 1 January 2027. This annual review, supported by fraud experts across Europe, ensures the taxonomy remains relevant to evolving fraud trends. Key updates in version 7.0 include replacing 'emotional manipulation' with more specific modi like 'support a friend or family member fraud', 'romance fraud', and 'charity / donation fraud'. Additionally, new labels for suspected money mule activity and 'card chip relay' fraud have been added. The taxonomy provides a simplified, pan-European framework for describing and categorising payment fraud scenarios, crucial for enhancing fraud monitoring, reporting, and information sharing, especially under the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation (PSR).
key_points: Version 7.0 effective date: 2027-01-01.
Updates reflect latest fraud trends, including new modi and labels.
Harmonises fraud classification for pan-European data sharing.
Supports information-sharing arrangements under forthcoming PSR.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI/CMIplus must prepare for the implementation of EBA Fraud Taxonomy v7.0 by 1 January 2027. This involves updating internal fraud detection and reporting systems to align with the new classifications and ensuring readiness for enhanced information sharing requirements under the future PSR.
